newsitem.title: EGYPT: Dealing system hinders trade on Cairo bourse.
newsitem.headline: Dealing system hinders trade on Cairo bourse.

text.p: Technical problems from a new dealing system hindered trade on the Cairo stock exchange on Monday, brokers said.
The stock market report was not available.
The exchange came to a complete standstill on Sunday after the bourse computer system crashed and was restored five minutes before the end of the session.
Sunday's volume was 5.79 million pounds ($1.70 million) -- its lowest level since early May -- and the Capital Market Authority's overall index fell 0.06 percent to 234.06 points.
About 70 percent of Monday's turnover came from trade of milling firms but their shares ended mostly down, brokers said.
"Most transactions were on the millers," Sherif Refaat of Thebes told Reuters. "Their prices went down because the demand was too heavy."
The market favourite Central and West Delta Flour Mills was the day's most active share but the stock ended down 0.25 pounds to 52.40. Shares worth 2.32 million pounds changed hands.
North Cairo Flour Mills ended unchanged at 109.50 pounds. Upper Egypt Flour Mills was down 0.70 pounds to 46.00. East Delta Flour Mills also fell 1.25 to finish at 37.00 pounds.
The housing sector was dominated by Heliopolis Housing and Development which brokers said reached 110.00 pounds.
"There was heavy demand for Heliopolis before the second tranche of shares goes on sale as reported," Hany el-Sayyed of El-Rashad Securities Brokerage said.
